diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Reza Goharzad said the US Congress does not have an effective leverage to limit Trump's decisions about continuing the war until the new representatives start their work. He added that in Trump's administration there is disagreement over continuing military operations, and JD Vance is trying to prevent the escalation of conflict by gaining support from anti-war Republicans. Meanwhile, Trump seeks to portray himself as the victor of the war and exit without admitting defeat.

Logan Kanapathi, a member of the Ontario Parliament, officially commemorated the victims of violent crackdowns in Iran and emphasized the province's solidarity with the Iranian community. He also appreciated the efforts of the non-profit organization "Memorial of Iran's Eternal Heroes" for seeking justice, recording narratives, and keeping the victims' names alive.

New Zealand's parliamentary election is taking place amid a very close competition between the two main parties. The latest polls show the National Party, led by the current Prime Minister, is only one percent ahead of the Labour Party, led by Chris Hipkins.

Katayoun Najafizadeh, head of the Iranian Organ Donation Association, announced that last year 130 children died on the waiting list at Rajaei Hospital due to the lack of available donor hearts. During the same period, only 30 pediatric heart transplants were performed at this hospital. Najafizadeh stated that the number of brain death cases in the country has not decreased, but the utilization rate of transplantable organs from brain-dead individuals remains unsatisfactory and below expectations.

Mohammadreza Mohseni Sani, a member of the National Security and Foreign Policy Commission of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, stated that Donald Trump's media actions and military movements by the US in the Sea of Oman do not matter to the Islamic Republic. He said that military attacks by the US and Israel have yielded no achievements and that US bases in West Asia have been destroyed. Mohseni Sani warned that any new conflict could have widespread consequences for various countries.

Ali-Asghar Nakhaei-Rad, a member of the Iranian parliament's Internal Affairs and Councils Commission, called for a review of the Islamic Republic's membership in the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), stating that this membership has only brought costs and restrictions. He criticized the International Atomic Energy Agency as influenced by the US and Western countries and said over 70 parliament members have signed a request to change Iran's nuclear doctrine. Nakhaei-Rad also accused the agency of transferring information about Iranian nuclear scientists and facilities to Israel and said leaving the NPT is separate from changing the nuclear doctrine.

Mohammad Akraminia, spokesperson for the Islamic Republic Army, warned that if the US attacks, the armed forces of the Islamic Republic will strike US targets without geographical limitation. He said that based on the order of Mojtaba Khamenei, all US targets, including bases outside Southwest Asia, will be targeted. Akraminia also emphasized that the only way to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is for the US to accept the seven conditions of the Islamic Republic.

Turkey moved one step closer to implementing the joint defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan by approving the "Mecca Pact" in parliament. However, sending Turkish military forces outside the country's territory still requires a separate parliamentary approval.

The 39th Tokyo International Film Festival ended with the presence of four Iranian filmmakers. During this edition, the works of these artists were showcased and the Akira Kurosawa Award was also given to Mohammad Rasoulof.

Rouhollah Rahimpour, journalist and political analyst, said Trump is under pressure from public opinion and Democrats to justify the necessity of war. He added that ambiguity about the Islamic Republic's nuclear program, proxy forces' activities, missile capabilities, and disruption in Strait of Hormuz shipping are among the issues Washington raises to justify the possible resumption of attacks.

Ali Akbar Velayati, advisor to the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic on international affairs, wrote on the social network X on Friday, November 6, 2026, that any energy or transit corridor that seeks to bypass the Islamic Republic will either be costly or unsustainable. He also wrote: 'Either collective security is achieved or everyone experiences collective insecurity.' Velayati said that the Islamic Republic is now one of the main architects of the regional order that cannot be removed or replaced.

A video on social media shows Erfan Esfandiari's family cutting his birthday cake in mourning. Erfan Esfandiari, 19 years old and one of the accused in the 'Alikhani Square' case in Isfahan, was executed on 28 Tir.

Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, Emir of Qatar, spoke on a phone call with Donald Trump, President of the United States, on Friday, 15 Aban, about diplomatic efforts to reduce regional tensions and achieve a comprehensive agreement to end the crisis. The two sides reviewed the latest regional developments and international efforts to reduce tensions. They also discussed the strategic relations between Qatar and the United States and ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation.

Ali Doraghi, a 60-year-old poet residing in Ahvaz, was arrested at his home by Intelligence Department agents on Tuesday, 12 Aban. Prior to the arrest, he was summoned to the Intelligence Department's news headquarters but could not attend due to heart disease. The agents eventually arrested him at his home and transferred him to an unknown location.

Marca reported that Jesus Ovono, the goalkeeper of Andorra, is in severe psychological shock after a fatal collision with Jesus de Miguel, a Tenerife player, and has not left his home since returning to Andorra. Gerard Pique, the main shareholder of the Andorra club, is personally following Ovono's mental state, and the club held an optional training session and a minute of silence after the death of Jesus de Miguel. The Spanish Footballers Association announced that Jesus Ovono will not be alone and psychological support is being provided to players of both teams.

Isaac Herzog, President of Israel, announced that he will introduce the person selected to form the new cabinet. Gadi Eizenkot received 67 recommendations from party representatives, and Benjamin Netanyahu received 46 recommendations at the end of consultations.
A video received shows that on the evening of 14 Aban in Tabriz, a citizen tore down a poster of Ali Khamenei titled "Martyr Leader" from the wall of a mosque.

Theo Francken, Belgium's defense minister, announced that the Islamic Republic tried to prevent Prince Reza Pahlavi's speech and warned that holding this meeting would have serious consequences. He said Tehran's opposition shows that the Islamic Republic is worried about Prince Reza Pahlavi's message and tries to restrict freedom of speech and research. Francken introduced Prince Reza Pahlavi as a main opposition figure to the Islamic Republic and said he supports forming a government based on free elections.

Shargh newspaper reported on sexual and verbal harassment of women in workplaces. Some women reported requests for personal photos during hiring, private questions, sexual jokes, unnecessary meetings, and disturbing messages outside work hours. Legal experts pointed to the lack of a clear mechanism to combat sexual harassment in Iran's labor law and obstacles to women's complaints.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, assessed Mohsen Rezaei's meeting with Vladimir Putin as part of Russia's mediation efforts to end the war. According to him, Moscow is trying to encourage the Islamic Republic to moderate its positions on 60% enriched uranium and the Strait of Hormuz and move toward a diplomatic solution. Aghaei added that this meeting could be Russia's last effort to warn the Islamic Republic before an escalation of conflicts.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said Trump will turn to foreign policy and increase pressure on the Islamic Republic to rebuild his political power and credibility after the Republicans' failure in the congressional elections. He added that Trump's emphasis on peace through power and maximum pressure, alongside the continuation of the Islamic Republic's positions, increases the likelihood of resuming military conflict.

A video shows that Javid Rezaei's mother placed her teenage son's clothes on his gravestone and cried in his memory. Javid Rezaei was killed by Islamic Republic agents during the January 8 protests in Zanjan at the age of 17.
Rainfall on the early morning of Friday, 15 Aban, caused flooding and problems for people in parts of eastern Mazandaran.

Some Iran International viewers criticized the Islamic Republic's foreign policy, the performance of government officials, and Mohsen Rezaei's role in the country's decision-making in response to his trip to Russia.

Prince Reza Pahlavi reported a meeting with Bernard Canten, Belgium's Minister of the Interior, where they discussed the increasing threats of the Islamic Republic against Belgium's security and its efforts to undermine the country's democracy. He also announced that he has asked Belgium to take a leading role in the European Union in confronting the Islamic Republic.

Prince Reza Pahlavi spoke about Middle East developments at the Royal Military Academy in Belgium on the last day of his trip to Brussels, invited by Theo Francken, Belgium's Defense Minister. Francken said the Islamic Republic threatened Belgium with severe consequences for hosting this speech, indicating Tehran's concern over Prince Reza Pahlavi's message. This report was provided by Lily Nikfar from Iran International.

The jury of the London criminal court has entered the decision-making phase after five weeks of hearing the case of three defendants accused of gathering information about Iran International journalists. Mostafa Sepahvand, Shapur Ghaleali-Khani Nouri, and Farhad Javadi-Mansh are accused of spying for the Islamic Republic with the aim of harming Mojtaba Pourmohsen and Kambiz Hosseini, journalists of Iran International.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said Trump tries to portray the war with the Islamic Republic as a defense of America. He referred to the killing of American soldiers in the 1983 attack on the Marine barracks in Beirut and the Islamic Republic's ideological positions against the US and Israel, saying Trump aims to prepare public opinion for resuming military operations.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International saying that to reduce costs, they intended to perform their car's periodic service personally, but faced a sharp and continuous increase in the prices of car consumables.

The head coach of Esteghlal spoke about the need for transfer windows to build an ideal Persepolis team, saying that the conditions of the fans must be understood as they always want wins and quality football. He added that a cohesive team should be built in the short term with a plan, and asked fans to support the teams without controversy or insults. Bakhtiari-Zadeh emphasized that Esteghlal is a big team and must show its best performance.

Reza Rezaei, CEO of Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad Water and Wastewater Company, announced that about 15 percent of the villages in the province, with a population close to 10,000 households, are facing water stress and drinking water supply problems. He said that in some villages, water resource shortages and in most areas, aging facilities and lack of water supply equipment are the main causes of this situation, and solving the problems depends on securing the necessary funding.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the Islamic Republic's seven conditions for negotiating with the US are designed to change the outcome of the war in favor of Tehran. He added that it is unlikely Washington will agree to them before resolving the Islamic Republic's nuclear program.

As the time approaches for the 2026 Friedrich Naumann Foundation Freedom Award to be given to Prince Reza Pahlavi, who will receive it on behalf of the people of Iran, a video has reached Iran International showing a citizen writing on a city wall: "From Iran to Germany, November 7, Long live the Shah."

New information received by Iran International indicates that the IRGC in Qazvin province had ordered shooting protesters before January 8. After the protests, the IRGC sent forces to schools to intimidate students to identify families of protesters. Seba Heydarkhani discusses the Qazvin protests in January in the Geography of the Iranian National Revolution program.

Videos released on social media show that a manager of the Artaban automotive group in Qazvin said that during the 40-day war, this factory was hit by a missile. He added that this factory was engaged in producing missile bodies for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Artaban Motor was the sponsor of Esteghlal Club in the last Premier League season, and their cooperation contract was signed in Mordad 1404.

Amirardalan Amiri was killed by bullets from the suppressive forces of the Islamic Republic during the Iranian people's revolution on 19 Dey in Vakilabad, Mashhad. His name remains in the memory of this land and his memory is a guiding light for freedom seekers.

The Trade Commission of the Iranian Writers' Association reported on the situation of writers and problems in the publishing industry after the war, noting ongoing censorship and violations of authors' rights. According to the report, censorship is applied not only before the first edition of books is published but also at various stages of printing. Asieh Amini, a social issues analyst, explains the pressure on writers and publishers to self-censor and its connection to economic conditions and the survival of the publishing industry.

A viewer sent a video message to Iran International addressing Iranians abroad: "On November 7 in Frankfurt, be the voice of the suffering and oppressed people of Iran." It is planned that on Saturday, 16 Aban, November 7, in Germany, Prince Reza Pahlavi will receive the 2026 Freedom Award from the Friedrich Naumann Foundation on behalf of the Iranian people.

Vahid Vidafar, a resident of Tabriz, was released from Tabriz prison on Monday, 11 Aban, after posting bail. His case hearing was held about two weeks ago via videoconference. He faces charges of "insulting the leader" and "starting espionage for Israel."

Ahmad Alamolhoda, the Friday prayer leader of Mashhad, said that the American hegemonic system no longer concerns democracy or republicanism and described both the Democratic and Republican parties as evil and impure. He added that changing the ruling party in the US makes no difference and both parties oppose the Islamic Republic. Alamolhoda emphasized that Democrats and Republicans in the US do not differ in their hostility towards the Islamic Republic.
According to the French newspaper Libération, on Friday, 15 Aban, four bomb threats against airplanes were recorded in France. On Thursday, at least 25 flights in Europe faced similar threats.

The Old Bailey court in London is handling the case of Ioannis Aidinidis, a Greek citizen accused of spying on an Iran International journalist for the Islamic Republic's intelligence service. He is accused of gathering information about this journalist.
A video received by Iran International shows a citizen removing the flag of the Islamic Republic that had been installed during government night gatherings in the city of Zahedan.
Today, Friday 15 Aban, several citizens from Qasr-e Qand in three villages, Kand, Chandukan, and Pask, were arrested by security forces and transferred to an unknown location.

Mohammad Atabak, Minister of Industry, Mining and Trade, requested a postponement of at least one year for the implementation of new vehicle standards in a letter to Mohammad Reza Aref. Atabak cited currency problems, the country's emergency conditions, and automakers' inability to invest in platform development as reasons for this request. If implemented, the upgrade of vehicle standards from 85 to 122 items and the fuel consumption improvement program will be delayed by one year.

Greek company Velos Tankers announced that a sailor died in an explosion likely caused by a missile attack on the tanker "MT Velos" in the Persian Gulf. The tanker, carrying petroleum products, was targeted on Thursday, 14 Aban while moving without cargo towards Bahrain. The sailor was initially reported missing after the explosion but his body was later found on the ship.

Mohammad Nabi Mousavi-Fard, the Friday prayer leader of Ahvaz, said in the Friday prayers on 15 Aban that missiles and military stockpiles are ready to destroy the enemy at the very first moments if they attack. He added that until the soldiers of the US and Israel are torn apart in the region, the flags of the armed forces will not fall. Mousavi-Fard also emphasized that the revolutionary nation and aerospace forces under the command of Seyed Qaed will not give an inch of land to the enemy.

Masoumeh Taherkhani, an economic analyst, said the government is gradually limiting the scope of beneficiaries of the ration card plan due to budget deficits and problems in securing resources for the ration card. She referred to a 412 trillion toman deficit in the ration card budget and said the government may eventually limit payments to the first and second income deciles.

A viewer sent a video message to Iran International saying that members of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, instead of addressing the livelihood crisis of the Iranian people, continuously think about solving Lebanon's problems and described this approach as "dishonesty."

Houthi forces supported by the Islamic Republic released images on Friday, 15 Aban, of operations against Yemeni government forces in the strategic Khabub mountain range, east of the Bab al-Mandab Strait. These clashes occur after the collapse of the ceasefire in Tir 1405, with Saudi Arabia and the Houthis carrying out reciprocal attacks. The Houthis had previously targeted airports, energy infrastructure, and military centers in Saudi Arabia.

Sepahan football team temporarily rose to the top of the Iranian Premier League standings with a 4-0 victory over Malavan in the twelfth week. Aluminium Arak also returned to winning ways after several weeks of failure by defeating Mes Shahr-e Babak 1-0. Malavan remained in 13th place with 10 points and Mes Shahr-e Babak stayed at the bottom of the table with five points.

Persepolis football team lost 2-1 to Fajr Sepasi in the twelfth week of the Premier League and lost the top spot. Fajr Sepasi took the lead with goals from Ehsan Pahlevan and Abolfazl Mordi, while Persepolis scored one own goal by Masoud Rigi. After the match, Persepolis fans chanted slogans against Mehdi Tartaar.

A report states that Mohammad Hossein-Zahi, a resident of Chabahar, has been held in an undisclosed security detention center for over 40 days. His arrest was carried out by the Intelligence Department forces in Chabahar county.

Mehdi Ghazanfari, former head of the National Development Fund, says that in the past five years, governments have withdrawn about 30 to 35 billion dollars from the fund's resources or reduced its share. The fund, which was supposed to preserve part of Iran's oil revenues for future generations, now faces tens of billions of dollars in unpaid claims from the government and the National Oil Company. Mehdi Beigi, a member of Iran International's editorial team, examines the fate of the wealth of future generations in the program "Pivast".

Videos published on social media show the accumulation of several dog carcasses in the cargo compartment of a pickup truck in the village of Ghasemabad, Rafsanjan. Some local residents have blamed the village management authorities, but the Ghasemabad village council has so far not responded and has not taken responsibility for the physical removal of the dogs.

Ali Kord, a member of the Social Commission of the Parliament, said that mediation by Qatar or Gulf countries is to deceive Iran and slows down their readiness. He added that before the attack on 9 Esfand last year, these countries with wrong diplomacy caused the joint attack by the US and Israel. Kord is not optimistic about the mediation unless the Qatari team clearly states in four languages that Iran has the right to defend itself, sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz, and has not committed aggression anywhere.

Ireland's state radio and television network, RTÉ, in Dublin was evacuated on Friday, November 6, after receiving a bomb threat email. This occurred as media newsrooms in Ireland and Bulgaria also received similar threats. The sender of these messages, who identified himself as "Mikhail Andropov," claimed responsibility for a widespread wave of hoax threats that have disrupted passenger flights across Europe.

According to HRANA news agency, Hamid Kazemi and Hassan Divand, two detainees from the January 2026 protests who are imprisoned in Karaj Central Penitentiary, were sentenced to death by the Second Branch of the Karaj Revolutionary Court. These two citizens were sentenced to death on charges of operational action and by invoking the intensification of the Islamic Penal Code.

The Canadian federal government introduced a plan in the 2026 budget to grant permanent residency to 200,000 temporary residents. At the same time, Ottawa has allocated 11.2 billion dollars in new military funding for the next five years.

The Times of Israel, citing two sources, reported that Islamic Republic negotiators are considering proposals that would lead to a significant reduction in US sanctions in exchange for limiting the nuclear program. An American official and a diplomat familiar with the matter told the outlet that Qatari mediators presented these proposals to the Iranian side in several rounds of talks over the past week in Tehran and Doha. According to them, Tehran had previously not even been willing to discuss the issue.

A video of a gas pipeline explosion in Gachsaran on Friday was sent to Iran International. The governor of this county said the explosion occurred during the execution of a municipal development project and was caused by a bulldozer hitting the pipeline.

Bloomberg reported that after months of deadlock in negotiations with the US, the Islamic Republic is considering Qatar's proposals regarding its nuclear activities; an action that could restart the stalled talks.

The Telegraph revealed in an exclusive report confidential documents showing that a secret committee in the parliament, before the war began, proposed strengthening military relations with Russia and China and developing air defense, missiles, and drones for the survival of the Islamic Republic. The newspaper disclosed that the Islamic Republic and Russia are negotiating an agreement to send advanced air defense systems to Tehran. The Telegraph wrote that Mojtaba Khamenei, leader of the Islamic Republic, sent Mohsen Rezaei to the Kremlin with a personal letter whose main request was the supply of the S-400 air defense system.

The defeat of the Republicans in the US midterm elections has increased discussions about the future of Pete Hegseth, the country's Secretary of Defense, and his responsibility in the war with the Islamic Republic. At the same time, a Republican member of Congress has called for Hegseth's impeachment.

Hassan Ameli, the Friday prayer leader of Ardabil, said on 15 Aban that the US election and Trump's humiliating defeat are part of God's revenge and the oppressed's revenge against the oppressor. He added that Trump is under severe criticism and reprimands and is dying every moment but cannot find death. Ameli attributed this situation to the blood of their martyred leader.

A group of Iranians on the route from Gothenburg to Frankfurt expressed support for Prince Reza Pahlavi, who is set to receive the 2026 Freedom Award from the Friedrich Naumann Foundation in Germany, and commemorated the martyrs of the national revolution.

In two work accidents at Rayan Polymer Pouya Company and a gypsum factory in Espiran, Tabriz, one worker died and two others were injured. Also, a well-digger worker in Mashhad was injured after falling into a well.

The Nobel Peace Center in Oslo was transformed into a realm of light on Thursday, 14 Aban, with light artworks by artists from across Europe. The fifth edition of the "Fjord Oslo" festival has illuminated buildings and public spaces in Norway's capital with large-scale light installations. This festival is part of the European cultural cooperation project "Imagining Peace," funded by the European Union.

In the past week, reports covered illegal hunting and wood smuggling in dozens of locations, sightings of cheetahs and leopards, air pollution especially in Khuzestan and Isfahan, leachate and sewage entering rivers, drought, and land subsidence. A total of 106 independent environmental news items were collected, including arrests, air quality records, wildlife observation and release, and other topics. This review is based on reports from various media and organizations.

Farhikhtegan reported with a video that Alireza Beiranvand is present at the national teams' camp. Mehdi Rajabzadeh, the coach of Fajr, said that whatever Beiranvand does is coordinated with the club and that he is currently injured and following up on his injury. Also, some Fajr Sepasi players reported Beiranvand's presence at the team hotel after the match with Persepolis.

BBC Verify, citing the British intelligence company Mayar, reported that satellite images show new excavation and construction at military bases in Garmdareh Karaj and Shahroud. The report mentions reconstruction at at least 12 other military sites, including missile and air bases damaged in US and Israeli attacks. Jim Lamson suggested the Shahroud excavations may be related to missile production, and a new entrance was identified in Karaj.

Published images show that a group of cinema actors, football figures, and sportspeople attended the memorial ceremony for the late Hamid Alidousti, former striker of Iran's national football team and Homa club, on Friday evening and expressed condolences to Taraneh Alidousti and her family. The wives of the late Nasser Hejazi and Ali Daei were also seen among the attendees. The ceremony was held at the Jame Mosque of Shahrak-e Gharb.

A motorcade carrying Lion and Sun flags traveled the streets of Frankfurt, Germany, on Friday, 15 Aban. The city is where Prince Reza Pahlavi is scheduled to receive the 2026 Freedom Award from the Friedrich Naumann Foundation on behalf of the Iranian people.

Donald Trump said that if the Islamic Republic had not been prevented from acquiring nuclear weapons, Israel and the entire Middle East would not exist today. On Friday, 15 Aban, he wrote on Truth Social that no one wants to say this but everyone knows it is true.
A report states that Diar Abron, a citizen from Piranshahr, was detained by security forces on 11 Aban. There has been no information about the location of this citizen's detention so far.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, wrote on X that they will not allow Trump to escape the region without cost or compensation. He also said their response to any mistake will be a decisive strike to free the largest US military base, Israel, once and for all. These statements were published on Friday, 15 Aban.

After Persepolis's home defeat against Fajr Sepasi in the twelfth week of the Premier League, the team's fans chanted against Mehdi Tartaar, demanding his departure. This was Persepolis's second home defeat and third loss in the Premier League. Mehdi Tartaar's team, which was leading the league before this match, fell 3 points behind Sepahan and lost the title race to Moharram Navidkia's team.

Mehdi Tartaar, Persepolis coach, accepted responsibility after his team's defeat against Fajr Sepasi and said that the pressure from the stands caused the players' failure to score. He criticized the fans' behavior and called for cheering until the 90th minute. Tartaar also said they follow the club's decision regarding team fines and hopes conditions improve with better results.
It was reported in the audio version of Harfe Akhar with Pouria Zeraati that Trump's order to start the heaviest military operation in the last ten years was mentioned.

On Friday, 15 Aban, a number of citizens in Shahroud held a march and protest demanding the closure of the bauxite mine in the city. According to these citizens, the continuation of the mine's activities has seriously endangered the region's water resources and environment.
It was reported in the audio version 24 with Fardad Farahzad that there is a security threat against Prince Reza Pahlavi in Germany.

A U.S. military official told Iran International that the United States is concerned about the safety and security of the people of Iran and urges them to stay home and keep away from IRGC forces and centers if military tensions escalate.

Forough Kenani, a sociology researcher and women's rights activist, said that despite the announcement of security restrictions on the presence of Prince Reza Pahlavi and his wife at the Frankfurt event, no changes have been made to the gathering's program so far. She considered this decision a sign of Germany's weak political will in confronting threats from the Islamic Republic. Kenani added that limiting Reza Pahlavi's presence weakens the voice of Iranians who cannot freely protest inside the country.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said Qatar's new plan to reduce tensions between Tehran and Washington, despite considering some demands of both sides, still remains distant from the conditions of the Islamic Republic and the nuclear demands of the US. He added that the Islamic Republic, by continuing to review this proposal, tries to delay the outbreak of war to benefit from political pressures on Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu. Rahimpour assessed the chances of reaching an agreement as low and said diplomatic efforts have not yet reduced the risk of the war restarting.

Iran International's exclusive investigation shows that the Islamic Republic has created a network to expand media influence using shell companies and cash payments through its embassy in the UK. More than 41,000 pounds were paid through a company in London to Ahmad Kabalo, a former Press TV journalist and founder of media such as African Stream and Sovereign Media. At least five former Press TV colleagues also work in these media to publish narratives aligned with Tehran.

Shahad Alavi, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said that the trial of three defendants accused of spying for the Islamic Republic with the aim of harming two Iran International journalists has ended in a London court, and the jury has entered the deliberation phase. He does not find the defendants' lawyers' defenses convincing and predicted that the jury will find the defendants guilty of serious charges, but the final decision has not yet been announced.

Yasmin Pahlavi said Frankfurt police officially informed them that they are not allowed to attend or speak at the Saturday gathering and will prevent their presence. The police cited threats from the Islamic Republic to violence and the possibility of participants being targeted as reasons for this decision. Yasmin Pahlavi considered this decision influenced by political considerations.

Domestic media reported early Saturday about hearing explosions and aircraft movement in Qeshm Island and Bandar Khamir. IRNA news agency, quoting eyewitnesses, stated that two projectiles hit the Suza area on Qeshm Island, but provincial sources have not yet explained the nature and details. Fars news agency confirmed hearing the explosions in Qeshm and Bandar Khamir and suggested this event might be related to a warning shot fired towards the Strait of Hormuz.

Prince Reza Pahlavi's press office announced that he will participate in the Friedrich Naumann Freedom Award ceremony and is determined to attend the Iranian gathering in Frankfurt afterward. The office said the gathering will proceed as planned. Earlier, his wife stated that German police prevented his speech at the gathering due to potential threats from the Islamic Republic.

Persepolis football team lost 2-1 to Fajr Sepasi in the twelfth week of the Premier League at Ghal'eh Hasan Khan Stadium. Mehdi Tartaar, the coach of the Reds, complained about Persepolis fans' chants against the players after the match.

Mohammad Taghavi analyzed the Persepolis - Fajr Sepasi match on the Hattrick program and said Persepolis has scored only one goal in the last three games, indicating a weak attack line. He also said the defense line situation of Persepolis is worrying.
Tasnim News Agency reported that according to initial reports, two missiles hit Qeshm Island. This report was published after sounds of explosions were heard in Qeshm and Bandar Khamir.

The international media office of the Qatari government denied reports of a failure in negotiations for an agreement between the US and the Islamic Republic, stating that those benefiting from ongoing war and instability in the region have deliberately distorted the statements of the Qatari Prime Minister to undermine diplomatic efforts. The statement emphasized that the Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Qatar announced that both sides are still striving to reach an agreement, and Qatari mediators remain in close coordination with the US and Iranian government to support ongoing negotiations.

Houshang Hassaniyari, a Middle East and military affairs expert, said that the arms cooperation between Russia and the Islamic Republic continues and its dimensions go beyond usual military deals. According to him, Moscow pursues long-term goals by delivering advanced equipment and expanding missile cooperation with Tehran, indirectly opposing the US. Hassaniyari added that Donald Trump's administration needs Russia to advance Ukraine peace talks and maintain a diplomatic channel with the Islamic Republic, while facing continued Russian military support for Tehran.

Sepahan football team fans set off fireworks during the match against Malavan at Naghsh-e Jahan Stadium in Isfahan on Friday, 15 Aban. They created an extraordinary atmosphere similar to scenes created by Borussia Dortmund fans at Signal Iduna Park stadium in Germany.

Donald Trump said in a speech at a NASA event in Florida that the US must remain the undisputed leader in superintelligence. He added that the US is about a year ahead of China and must win. Trump also warned that sometimes superintelligence is too smart and it might be necessary to reduce its level.

The Hengaw Human Rights Organization reported that five citizens arrested during the nationwide protests of Dey 1404 were sentenced to a total of 25 years of imprisonment by the First Branch of the Revolutionary Court of Semnan. Each of these individuals was sentenced to five years of imprisonment on charges of "acting against national security." These five have been held in Semnan Central Prison since their arrest and have been deprived of leave and legal facilities.

Donald Trump said that a small air defense system in Qeshm was destroyed within about 15 minutes. Two missiles hit Qeshm Island early Saturday. Trump added that they are engaging with Iran and have made progress, and he does not consider the situation a war.

NBC News reported, citing American officials, that some of Donald Trump's advisors have told him that the window for resuming large-scale military operations in Iran is closing. These officials added that Trump's advisors have urged him to act before the new Congress convenes in January 2027, and that resuming large-scale military operations in Iran requires Trump to make his decision within the next few weeks.

The Wall Street Journal reported increased pressure from Trump's advisors to influence his decisions; the disagreements are over continuing diplomacy, resuming military operations, and intensifying economic pressure against Iran.

Fouad Pashaei, Secretary-General of the Iranian Constitutional Party, said the gathering of Iranians in Frankfurt will be held tomorrow despite threats and efforts to cancel Prince Reza Pahlavi's speech. After widespread protests by Iranians against the German police's actions to cancel the event, the police agreed to secure the gathering with increased security measures and higher costs. Pashaei also considered the continuation of protests by Iranians abroad for over ten months as a serious and ongoing sign of opposition to the Islamic Republic.

A group of independent UN experts, including Mai Sato, the Special Rapporteur on human rights in Iran, condemned the increase in personal attacks and threats against the organization's reporters and emphasized that intimidation will not silence them. These experts expressed concern about the rise in insults and threats from some governments and other actors in a statement released on Friday, 15 Aban in Geneva, but did not name any specific country. They called for support from UN officials and cooperation from governments with the reporters.

Farzin Nadimi said the US warning message to the Iranian people does not necessarily mean an imminent military attack, but it can be a warning to the Islamic Republic about the seriousness of a possible military action. He added that the deployment of IRGC and Basij military bases in residential areas limits US operations and may slow down the operation speed. Nadimi said the US aims with these warnings to reduce civilian casualties and prevent the Islamic Republic from using people as human shields.
